study.title: High-throughput property-driven generative design of functional organic molecules
study.citation: Westermayr J, Gilkes J, Barrett R, Maurer RJ. Nature Computational Science 3, 139-148 (2023).
study.workflow_type: Iterative property-biased G-SchNet generation with SchNet+H screening and synthetic-complexity filtering
study.assessment_scope: Published article, Supplementary Information, data and code availability statements, and linked public records; the analysis was not rerun. Converted to version 1.0.0 identifiers from the version 0.2.0 audit of 2026-07-20.

items.summary: The OE62 dataset and molecular scope are named, and disconnected structures, duplicates, and molecules with unpaired electrons are excluded. Licence information can be recovered from the linked OE62 and generated-data records. Exact split manifests and a predeclared molecular matching rule with a cross-split collision rate are not provided.
Two SchNet+H models use different random train/test splits for the committee calculation, but the split sizes, grouping rationale, model-selection use, and G-SchNet split manifests are not stated.
source_locations: Supplementary Section 3, "Validation of molecules at the edges of the distributions"

items.summary: The autoregressive three-dimensional G-SchNet representation and principal hyperparameters are specified, including batch size 2, a 10 Å cutoff, 128 features, nine interaction blocks, 25 Gaussian functions, and five sampled atom placements per molecule. Random seeds are not stated.

The initial learning rate, decay rule, batch size, and approximate duration of one generation-screening loop are reported. SchNet+H hardware is identified, but the final epoch count, precision, and matched training wall-clock statistics are not all provided.
source_locations: Methods, "G-SchNet model for molecule generation" and "Computational details of the workflow for targeted design"

items.summary: Each loop generates 200,000 molecules for gap, electron-affinity, and multi-property experiments and 100,000 for ionisation-potential and knockout experiments. Molecules are filtered for structural validity, sorted by predicted properties, and selected relative to the loop mean and standard deviation before retraining; the 70-atom restriction introduced for ionisation-potential generation is also stated. Inference throughput is not given separately from the duration of a complete loop.
source_locations: Methods, "Computational details of the workflow for targeted design"

items.summary: Target-property distributions, valid molecule counts, chemical-diversity analyses, committee disagreement, and higher-level electronic-structure checks are reported. The study does not provide a formal molecular novelty definition, a single stagewise metric record, or uncertainty across independent generative runs.
source_locations: Supplementary Sections 1-4, Supplementary Figs. 1-11, and Supplementary Data 1

items.summary: SCScore is used as a 1-5 proxy for synthetic complexity and is computed from canonical SMILES generated with Open Babel. The study does not include retrosynthesis tool settings, a route-level success criterion, or experimental synthesis validation.
source_locations: Methods, "SCScore to predict the complexity of synthesizability of molecules"

items.summary: Knockout experiments and comparisons between single- and multi-property biasing test parts of the workflow. A matched random, retrieval, virtual-screening, or simple non-deep-learning baseline under the same evaluator budget is not reported.

Iterative selection thresholds, two-model committee uncertainty, variable loop counts, and a qualitative stopping rule are described. The study monitors property distributions and chemical diversity, and terminates each experiment once the property distribution no longer changes significantly. The stopping tolerance is not numerical and the complete evaluator budget is not collected in one record.
source_locations: Methods, "Computational details of the workflow for targeted design"

items.summary: Generated data, electronic-structure calculations, modified G-SchNet and SchNet+H code releases, archived versions, and tutorials are linked. The paper does not identify an environment lockfile, split checksums, a complete determinism record, or one command that rebuilds the reported figures and tables.

One loop takes approximately two days; the base G-SchNet training and subsequent biasing times are described; and the CPU and GPU systems used for quantum-chemistry calculations and SchNet+H predictions are identified. Candidate throughput uncertainty and energy or carbon estimates are not reported.
source_locations: Methods, "Computational details of the workflow for targeted design"

items.summary: The study targets electronic properties of small organic molecules and does not expose a hazardous target, autonomous execution pathway, or access mechanism that makes a governance control material to the reported claim. Dataset and code licences are assessed under Data and Reproducibility.
source_locations: main article, "Workflow" and Data and Code availability

items.summary: Candidate counts, valid counts, loop numbers, validation subsets, and approximate compute are available, but they are distributed across the article, Supplementary Information, and Supplementary Data rather than assembled as a single attrition and budget summary.
source_locations: Methods, "Computational details of the workflow for targeted design"
